message.content:
The sculpture that most people think of when they picture the 19th‑century art world is **Auguste Rodin’s “The Kiss” (1889)**. Rodin had already made a name for himself with works such as *The Gates of Hell* and *The Burghers of Calais*, but it was *The Kiss* that captured the public imagination on a scale that rivaled even his later masterpiece, *The Thinker*. **Why it stands out** | Feature | Details | |---------|---------| | **Date** | 1889 (first cast) | | **Style** | Realist/Impressionist blend – a tender, almost tactile rendering of two lovers embracing | | **Impact** | • Widely reproduced in bronze, marble, and other media
• Became a symbol of romantic love in popular culture
• Influenced countless artists and designers | | **Legacy** | • Still one of the most frequently displayed and sold sculptures worldwide
• Its image appears on postcards, calendars, and even in advertising | While other 19th‑century masterpieces—such as *The Gates of Hell*, *The Burghers of Calais*, or *The Death of Sardanapalus*—are celebrated within art history circles, *The Kiss* is the work that most people recognize instantly, making it the de facto “most famous” sculpture of that era.
